messages:
eric: Hey folks  day 1 WSL weirdness. Using Windows 11 with WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04). I installed asdf under WSL and added nodejs 18 + python 3.11. npm/pip install native modules fail with OpenSSL/clang errors and VS Code Remote - WSL terminal doesn't see my REPO_TOKEN env var from my Windows profile. Also my SSH key lives in Pageant on Windows  how do I make git/ssh in WSL use it so I can clone org/private repos? Any checklists?

molly: welcome! WSL has a few moving parts. Short checklist: 1) install build deps in Ubuntu (build-essential, libssl-dev, pkg-config, zlib1g-dev), 2) ensure asdf is sourced in ~/.profile (WSL default login file), 3) VS Code Remote-WSL session inherits Linux envs not Windows env, so set tokens in WSL or use the Remote settings to forward envs.

eric: ugh okay what exact apt packages?

harry: I usually run:```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev pkg-config zlib1g-dev libffi-dev python3-dev
# source asdf in ~/.profile
echo ". $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh" >> ~/.profile
source ~/.profile
asdf plugin-add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git || true
asdf install nodejs 18.16.0
asdf global nodejs 18.16.0
```
That fixes most node-gyp/pip build problems. If you rebuilt python via asdf before the libs, re-install the asdf python version so it links properly.

eric: got node/pip builds working, thanks. Now SSH/Pageant  can WSL use the Windows agent?

molly: Two options: 1) use a native Linux key in WSL and run ssh-agent there, or 2) forward Pageant to WSL via a small helper like 'wsl-ssh-pageant' or the built-in Windows OpenSSH agent socket. We use the latter internally sometimes. Example for using the Windows agent socket in WSL:```bash
# in WSL ~/.ssh/config
Host *
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  ForwardAgent yes

# create Windows agent socket symlink (PowerShell: setx WSLENV SSH_AUTH_SOCK/up)
# or use wslu package's wslview/wslvar to expose the socket
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$(wslvar.exe -s SSH_AUTH_SOCK 2>/dev/null || true)
```
If you prefer a pure WSL key, `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and add to your .profile so agent starts on login. Pageant bridging works but needs the helper tool installed on Windows.

eric: I tried `wsl-ssh-pageant` and it worked after adding `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/tmp/wsl-ssh-agent.sock` to ~/.profile. Git clones now use my key.

eric: last bit: REPO_TOKEN and REDWOOD_DEV envs  best place to put them so VS Code Remote-WSL terminals see them but they don't leak into Windows world?

hmolly: Put them in WSL-only secrets. We prefer direnv + the Linux keyring (libsecret) or store secrets in ~/.local/share/keyrings and load via a small loader. Minimal approach: keep them in ~/.profile but ensure ~/.profile is not synced to dotfiles repo. Example `.profile` snippet:```bash
export REDWOOD_DEV=1
export REPO_TOKEN="$(secret-tool lookup service redwood repo-token)"
```
If you must keep a file, use a local-only `.envrc` with direnv and add it to .gitignore. Then `direnv allow` will load it into WSL shells and VS Code Remote-WSL.

eric: what's the recommended dotfiles flow for WSL? I don't want to overwrite Windows configs.

hmolly: clone org/dotfiles-starter into WSL home and use stow to symlink only the unix-friendly parts (bash/zsh, gitconfig, asdf configs). Don't symlink Windows paths. We usually have a README section "WSL notes" that shows which stow packages are safe. Example:```bash
git clone git@github.com:org/dotfiles-starter.git ~/dotfiles-starter
cd ~/dotfiles-starter
stow zsh git asdf
```
Keep any Windows-specific helpers in a separate repo or in a local-only folder.

eric: sweet  remote-WSL now sees REPO_TOKEN via direnv and ssh clones work. Any VS Code tips?

hmolly: launch VS Code with the Remote - WSL extension and open the folder in WSL (`code .` from WSL shell). That ensures the integrated terminal and extensions run in the Linux environment and see your asdf shims. If extensions run on the Windows side accidentally, check the bottom-left of VS Code for the "WSL: Ubuntu" badge.
